title: Upstream hint sketches + on-demand diagnostic snapshotter to reduce hotpath tracing overhead
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Reduce tracer hotpath cost by moving expensive metadata and exemplar payload work off the synchronous path. We will add a tiny upstream hint sketch that captures low-cost signals to guide sampling decisions and an external diagnostic snapshotter that can be triggered (probabilistically or on-demand) to reconstruct full traces for retained tail events.
background: Production services report increased p95 CPU and allocations attributed to inline exemplar marshaling and span metadata enrichment. Prior art at Redwood includes deferred encoding and microbatch emission; this ticket explores a paired approach: (1) upstream constant-size hint sketches that allow aggressive lightweight sampling, and (2) an async diagnostic snapshotter to reconstruct full context for selected samples without adding hotpath allocations.
design_decisions: Use a fixed-size, bloom-ish sketch (64-256 bytes) attached at ingress to carry minimal signals (route id, latency bucket, tenant id hash, anomaly bit)
Make the sketch cheap to produce: stack-allocated, single memcopy, avoid heap allocations in hotpath
Sampler consumes sketches and uses a small windowed credit bank per-tenant to decide retention probability; sketches influence tail-priority multiplier
When a sketch is marked for enrichment, emit a tiny pointer to the diagnostic snapshot service via an async queue rather than embedding heavy payloads in the hotpath

Diagnostic snapshotter will perform on-demand rehydration by fetching associated logs/metrics/span-chunks from long-tail buffers and, if needed, request synchronous agent-side dumps via a backchannel with strict rate limits
Expose opt-in per-route and per-tenant controls in the Console to tune sketch aggressiveness and snapshot budgets
implementation_plan: Add sketch generation helper in ingress proxy (C++) and language SDK shims (Go/Node) - week 1
Implement sketch consumer and credit bank sampler in central sampling service (Rust) with feature flag - week 2
Build diagnostic snapshotter service (Python/Go) with bounded queue and replay worker - week 3
Hook enrichment queue to existing long-tail storage (logs/kv-cache) with rate-limited agent dump backchannel - week 4
Add Console controls and charts for sketch traffic, snapshot budget, and enrichment success rate - week 4
Rollout on canary, monitor CPU/alloc and tail-capture fidelity, then ramp - week 5
tasks: ENG: add sketch struct + ingress hook (PR: github.com/redwood/ingress-proxy/pull/?)
ENG: sampling service: credit-bank and sketch-driven policy (PR: github.com/redwood/sampling/pull/?)
ENG: snapshotter service + replay worker (PR: github.com/redwood/diagnostics/pull/?)
SRE: deploy snapshotter to staging with circuit breaker and quota
DX: Console controls + dashboards (design doc link below)
QA: synthetic tail injection harness and fidelity tests
acceptance_criteria: Hotpath CPU allocations from tracer decreased by >= 35% on sampled services (measured via flame graphs)
End-to-end p95 latency of critical inference path not regressed beyond 1% at baseline traffic
Tail capture fidelity: diagnostic snapshotter must reconstruct >= 90% of contextual fields (headers, last-10-logs, model request blob) for enriched events in tests
Snapshotter queue must respect configured budget; no service > burst budget for 10 consecutive minutes
Feature flagged and defaulted to off; canary rollout to two services with no user-impact incidents
rollout_plan: Start behind feature flag. Canary on two low-risk services (ingest-service, redis-proxy) for 72 hours. Gradually enable for tenant segments using Circuit Breaker: 0.1% -> 1% -> 5% -> 25% -> global over 7 days, with automated rollback on any of: CPU allocation increase >10% over baseline, snapshot worker error rate >2%, or failure to reconstruct >20% of snapshots.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Diagnostic snapshotter might not find enough context to reconstruct -> Mitigation: keep short-lived ring buffer on agents for last-5-logs and KV-chunks, configurable retention
Risk: Sketch incompatibility across SDK versions -> Mitigation: graceful fallback where unknown sketch version treated as 'no hint', safe defaults
Risk: Snapshotter surge causing cost spike -> Mitigation: strict tenant quotas and per-tenant budget enforcement in sampling service
Risk: Added complexity in sampling decisions -> Mitigation: preserve simple default policy and expose advanced sketch-driven policy behind flag
